comment:
* Implementation of the {@link android.support.v4.internal.view.SupportMenu} interface for creating a
 * standard menu UI.
 *
 * @hide

variables.name: mQwertyMode
variables.comment:
* Whether the shortcuts should be qwerty-accessible. Use isQwertyMode() instead of accessing
     * this directly.

variables.name: mShortcutsVisible
variables.comment:
* Whether the shortcuts should be visible on menus. Use isShortcutsVisible() instead of
     * accessing this directly.

variables.name: mCallback
variables.comment:
* Callback that will receive the various menu-related events generated by this class. Use
     * getCallback to get a reference to the callback.

variables.name: mItems
variables.comment: * Contains all of the items for this menu

variables.name: mVisibleItems
variables.comment:
* Contains only the items that are currently visible.  This will be created/refreshed from
     * {@link #getVisibleItems()}

variables.name: mIsVisibleItemsStale
variables.comment:
* Whether or not the items (or any one item's shown state) has changed since it was last
     * fetched from {@link #getVisibleItems()}

variables.name: mActionItems
variables.comment: * Contains only the items that should appear in the Action Bar, if present.

variables.name: mNonActionItems
variables.comment: * Contains items that should NOT appear in the Action Bar, if present.

variables.name: mIsActionItemsStale
variables.comment:
* Whether or not the items (or any one item's action state) has changed since it was last
     * fetched.

variables.name: mDefaultShowAsAction
variables.comment: * Default value for how added items should show in the action list.

variables.name: mCurrentMenuInfo
variables.comment:
* Current use case is Context Menus: As Views populate the context menu, each one has extra
     * information that should be passed along.  This is the current menu info that should be set on
     * all items added to this menu.

variables.name: mHeaderTitle
variables.comment: * Header title for menu types that have a header (context and submenus)

variables.name: mHeaderIcon
variables.comment: * Header icon for menu types that have a header and support icons (context)

variables.name: mHeaderView
variables.comment: Header custom view for menu types that have a header and support custom views (context)

variables.name: mFrozenViewStates
variables.comment:
* Contains the state of the View hierarchy for all menu views when the menu
     * was frozen.

variables.name: mPreventDispatchingItemsChanged
variables.comment:
* Prevents onItemsChanged from doing its junk, useful for batching commands
     * that may individually call onItemsChanged.

variables.name: mExpandedItem
variables.comment: * Currently expanded menu item; must be collapsed when we clear.

variables.name: mOverrideVisibleItems
variables.comment: * Whether to override the result of {@link #hasVisibleItems()} and always return true

methods.comment:
* This function will return all the menu and sub-menu items that can
     * be directly (the shortcut directly corresponds) and indirectly
     * (the ALT-enabled char corresponds to the shortcut) associated
     * with the keyCode.

methods.name: MenuItemImpl findItemWithShortcutForKey(int keyCode, KeyEvent event)
methods.comment:
* We want to return the menu item associated with the key, but if there is no
     * ambiguity (i.e. there is only one menu item corresponding to the key) we want
     * to return it even if it's not an exact match; this allow the user to
     * _not_ use the ALT key for example, making the use of shortcuts slightly more
     * user-friendly. An example is on the G1, '!' and '1' are on the same key, and
     * in Gmail, Menu+1 will trigger Menu+! (the actual shortcut).
     *
     * On the other hand, if two (or more) shortcuts corresponds to the same key,
     * we have to only return the exact match.

methods.name: public void flagActionItems()
methods.comment:
* This method determines which menu items get to be 'action items' that will appear * in an action bar and which items should be 'overflow items' in a secondary menu. * The rules are as follows: * *

Items are considered for inclusion in the order specified within the menu. * There is a limit of mMaxActionItems as a total count, optionally including the overflow * menu button itself. This is a soft limit; if an item shares a group ID with an item * previously included as an action item, the new item will stay with its group and become * an action item itself even if it breaks the max item count limit. This is done to * limit the conceptual complexity of the items presented within an action bar. Only a few * unrelated concepts should be presented to the user in this space, and groups are treated * as a single concept. * *

There is also a hard limit of consumed measurable space: mActionWidthLimit. This * limit may be broken by a single item that exceeds the remaining space, but no further * items may be added. If an item that is part of a group cannot fit within the remaining * measured width, the entire group will be demoted to overflow. This is done to ensure room * for navigation and other affordances in the action bar as well as reduce general UI clutter. * *

The space freed by demoting a full group cannot be consumed by future menu items. * Once items begin to overflow, all future items become overflow items as well. This is * to avoid inadvertent reordering that may break the app's intended design.
